From: Mike Haine, LEAMINGTON

Dear Eds.. SAM is superb! OUTLET
on SAM excels!

Nice to see the beginnings of
SAMCLASS.Perhaps Stephen Wilson
can help with a paging problem.
In my version of TABLOID for SAM
(Just sent off to Brian), I need
to access the screen buffer
since my prog uses a screen copy
technique. To do this I put a
short routine at 4004h:-

EX (SP),HL : LD (4800H),HL :
LD A,14 : OUT(251),A :
LD HL,8000H : LD DE, 4000H :
LD BC,O800H : LDIR :
LD HL,(4800H): LD A,2 :
OUT (251),A : EX (SP),HL:RET

Briefly this aims to store the
value in the stack pointer; page
the screen buffer page into the
HMPR; COPY the bytes from the
top 8 lines of the screen into
4000h to 47ffh; page back the
original LMPR; recover sp and
Return to the calling point.

This works fine if the routine
is called from BASIC but if the
call is made from m/c SAM
resets. Suggestions welcome. How
about it Stephen? Correspondence
on SAM very welcome.

Mike Haine, Riverside,Welsh Road
Offchurch, LEAMINGTON CV33 9AH

> Mike Haine from Stephen Wilson

 [Stephen Wilson is our SAM-
 CLASS programming expert.
 Readers may also write direct
 to him at 41 Warrix Avenue,
 Irvine,Ayrshire,Scotland KA12
 0DW for programming help.]

Thanks for the letter, Mike.

Looking at your routine, I can
see you understand the paging
principle, but there are quite a
few (serious), bugs in your
program:

Your routine is stored at #4004
so going through your program:
you store the value pointed to
by the Stack Pointer.

Although,I don't see why - the
stack isn't affected during
paging unless its being paged!
at #4800, then page the screen
into High Mem (32768-65535).

You then say you copy the top 8
lines into #4000! - here is the
bug (or is it intentional!). You
are writing #800 bytes into
#4000, and the routine to do it
is at #4004 - the routine will
be overwritten! (Remember HL=
store, DE=DEstination, BC =
length), furthermore,you say you
want the top 8 lines - a line is
128 bytes in length (Modes 3
+4),8 of these = 1024 bytes or
#400. You then page back the
value of the HMPR: The original
value is 1 not 2!

(SAMCO use the following page no
i.e: Page No=INT
(address/16384)-1 so you see
(32768/16384)=2-1=1 just like
the screen=245760
(245760/16384)=15-1=14!

You say the routine works from
BASIC - it will, but once the
LDIR has been executed,the bytes
where the LDIR was,is now a copy
of the lines, so now the Z80
starts to execute this data!
This is why it may crash, but in
BASIC it may hit a 201, and
return or something, I'm not
exactly sure.

Anyway, here's my alternative,
hope it helps! - and I hope I
have as well!

     SCREEN:EQU #8000
 COPYBUFFER:EQU #7000
  CODESTART:EQU #4000
     LENGTH:EQU #0400

10  ORG CODESTART
20  LD HL,TEMPSPSTORE
30  EX (SP),HL
40  OUT (251),A
50  LD HL,SCREEN
60  LD DE,COPYBUFFER
70  LD BC,LENGTH
80  LDIR
90  LD A,1
100 OUT (251),A
110 LD HL,TEMPSPSTORE
120 EX (SP),HL
130 RET
140 TEMPSPSTORE:DW 0

This sets up a buffer at #7000
to act as a store for the lines
you have copied. The code is at
#4000 and you can store the
value at SP, in TEMPSPSTORE. -
Watch where your LDIR ends:you
stored your (SP) at #4800,it may
be overwritten! Watch where your
stack is while paging,especially
if its near a boundary- remember
not to load your code straight
into 16384 - the system will
crash because you'll have over-
written quite a few important
stores,like the stack, and the
SYS Vars.

        - Stephen Wilson

From: George Robson, WEST YORKS.

First I'd like to congratulate
you on your excellent production
of OUTLET.

Although I am by no means a
computer expert (I shall be 70
next month) I have enjoyed
dabbling with games and graphics
for a number of years.

I started with 16k Spectrum and
went up through all the versions
ending up with a +3. I now also
have a Sam Coupe. I look forward
to receiving the monthly edition
of OUTLET, and although some of
the items are far too advanced
for my limited knowledge, I like
the utilities and the excellent
screen shots.

Now I wonder if I may ask a
couple of questions.
 1)This may sound very simple to
most people but I would like to
know the correct method to SAVE
a single item from an OUTLET
disc to another disc? By using
DIR1 I can get a list of the
items on the disc, and if the
program has only a single entry
on it, I can first LOAD it, then
BREAK and then SAVE onto another
disc and this works O.K. It is
the program which consists of a
number of directory entries
which I can't fathom out. e.g.
in OUTLET 40 there was an
'SC.COMPRESSOR" utility. The
entries in the directory were
  9 SC.COMP. 14 BASIC 9000
 51 SC.COMP.S   49 SCREEN$
 65 SC.COMP.C CODE 31882,630

If I just LOAD the program from
the OUTLET index, then BREAK and
SAVE - all that is saved is the
BASIC section. If I SAVE each of
the directory entries in
turn (i.e. 9 + 51 + 65) then
RUN - still no joy on reloading.
Should I be doing something
else? Please tell me the secret!

 2) I don't know if this query
has been dealt with before (I
only have OUTLET from SAM issue
37).  When a Spectrum game is
loaded into the Sam Coupe the
control menu is usually
displayed.  One should select
"SINCLAIR" or "INTERFACE II" for
joystick control. However, on a
few games I notice that although
the movements work O.K. (e.g.
Left, Right, Up, Down) the Fire


button doesn't. The Fire command
is usually on the keyboard at
number 0. Sometimes, using the
"REDEFINE" keys can get it to
work on the joystick, but very
rarely.  I wondered if there is
any way to correct this fault as
it is most awkward using the
joystick for movements yet
having to use the 0 key for
Fire.  I asked SAMCO about this
and they knew that it happened
with some games but couldn't
give any idea of how to cure it.

Hoping you can assist me.

Keep up the good work.

        Yours faithfully,

          George Robson

Brian Cavers to George Robson

I've not come across this joy-
stick problem before. I have
heard that auto-fire does not
work with the Sinclair method of
reading a joystick but I've not
heard of FIRE failing on its
own when the directions all
work.Can you name the games? Has
anyone else any ideas?

SC_COMPRESSOR loads the code up
to address 84000 (see line 9000)
so you need to save it as CODE
84000,630 if you are SAVEing it
after having loaded the program.
Alternatively, enter LOAD 65 and
then save as CODE 31882,630. A
much easier way to copy files is
to use COPY "NAME" TO "NAME".

However, by FAR the easiest way
is to get CATLOADER (OUTLET 33).
It will list all the files on a
disc on-screen and you select
any you want to copy. It has a
whole host of other features of
course. I use it all the time.

                        - Brian

From: Ettrick Thomson, SUFFOLK

Simon Greenfield (Outlet 43,
More Mail p.22) says "Kwikcal
(Outlet 41)gives...wrong dates".
I think his copy of the program
must have been corrupted or
something.

The program works for any year.
I have checked 1990,1991,1992
and also seven dates between
1798 and 1815, for which I
happen to have the days of the
week. All O.K.

The program works not only for
the present Gregorian calendar,
adopted in England in 1752, but
also for the previous Julian
Calendar.

If you try Feb 1700,you will see
that that was regarded as a Leap
Year. Sep.1752, when the change-
over took place, shows the 11
days that were "lost". These 11
days still persist in that the
Treasury refused to accept the
associated change, whereby the
year began on 1 Jan instead of
25 March -refusing to lose their
11 days.So,25 March, with the 11
days"restored" became 6 April (a
date we income-tax payers know
well.         - Ettrick Thomson

Sorry to both you and Simon! The
page with my reply on this went
walkabout last month! I sussed
the answer is that Simon entered
91 as the year instead of 1991
so he got the calender for AD91!
                        - Brian

To Bill Clarke from Brian Gaff.

I gather you phoned about a
suitable cable to connect a 128K
to a +3 Spectrum. I assume you
mean one for the RS232 ports.
Well, apparenly Brockhill
Enterprises can supply the
cables and plugs, though you may
need to wire them yourself.

This should be easy enough
though as TXD will go to RXD and
CTS to DTR, in both cases. You
will need a program like FIDO128
in both machines.[In ADDENDERS!]

The data is loaded into the
buffer of one machine and, when
it is in terminal mode, symbol
shift U is pressed.

The receiving machine is put in
terminal mode, and when symbol
shift I is pressed, the borders
should pulse blue, as the data
transfers. It is just a case of
saving the data from the buffer
after that.

I hope this is what you meant,
as I got your query second hand!
Brockhill are on 07683 72027.

                         - B.G.

From: Terry Clark, TROWBRIDGE

In Outletters No.41 I see you'd
like to use your Atari mouse on
the Sam. This can be done but
unless you have loads of junk,
like me,it could cost about `30.
I have been using both Atari and
Genius units for some twelve
months without ill-effect.

The old type Datel interface,
supplied with Artist 2 from the
old +48, was adapted with vero-
board and wire to the Sam DIN
connector as a one to one using
only the lines needed by the
interface. A modified Maplin-
Amstrad mother-board enables
addition of Sam Comms, Music
Maker and Vidi ZX when required.

This set up works well for home
grown programs, reading IN 64479
for horizontal, IN 65503 for
vertical, IN 64223 for buttons.

The Lerm/Artist2 works normally
and screens are loaded into
Flash for colour and tidy up.

If you decide to experiment I'd
be grateful for any information
on adapting to Flash.

Thanks for supporting the Sam,
without Outlet it would have
ended up in the dustbin, as I
have no interest in games. The
articles,demos and programs have
revived my enthusiasm.

Many thanks for an entertaining
mag.             T.C.

To Terry Clark from Brian Gaff

I was very interested to hear of
your hardware adaptations for
the SAM. I -in the guise of B.G.
Services -was thinking of making
a port converter to let Spectrum
add-ons be used on SAM.

However, SAMCO were not too keen
as there could be some inter-
faces which may cause damage to
the ASIC if connected. I do have
a prototype running though.

I gather that the SAM mouse will
be strictly for SAM, it is a
pity that they cannot just make
an interface and let the user
use a cheap serial mouse as you
have done.

From: Simon Greenfield, LINCOLN

I've just read a letter about a
reader in Issue 42 who says he
can't get his MGT Lifetime drive
3.5" to work on his +3 except in
48k mode, and that it only
formats to 178k (173 actually).
This is true but he should have
received from MGT a utility disc
called '+3 DISCMATE' which will
format a disc to 706K, and it
contains other useful utilities
for the +3.

This software was done by your
man Brian Gaff (but don't hold
me to that). As to getting the
drive to work in +3 BASIC mode I
found that you need to set the
dip switches as the following:-

     AMSTRAD + IBM - DRIVE B
   1    2    3    4    5    6

  OFF   ON   ON   OFF  ON   OFF

As stated on the last page of
the Drives User manual, which I
agree is poorly documented, and
the part MGT fail to mention is
first switch on the +3 then the
drive. Now insert a disk into
the LIFETIME drive and press the
+3's reset button. The drive's
light should come on now and
when you are back to the +3 main
menu you should have underneath
on the bottom line telling you
DRIVES A,B AND M AVAILABLE. The
drive can now be used in +3
BASIC mode. If not re-do the
whole procedure over again.

This method of inserting a disk
into the drive then pressing the
reset button for the drive to be
acknowledged is a bit like play-
ing a video recorder in that
when you press PLAY on the VCR
with no tape in you get nothing
but If you insert a tape then
press PLAY - Bob's your uncle!

I'd like to point out that I've
now upgraded to a '512k system
SAM' and also I am now using the
excellent MASTERDOS which,by the
way, is similar to the ADFS dos
on the Acorn Electron except
it's better, more powerful, and
a darn sight easier to use. Not
that I have an Electron but know
someone who does and he pulls
his hair out a lot, especially

now he's seen what my MASTERDOS
can do plus more, like other
users of this new Dos.I strongly
recommend every SAM owner to buy
this, as it is one hell of an
improvement over the old SAMdos.

You may be interested to know
that Dave Tonks, editor of SAM
SUPPLEMENT, has found a way to
transfer AMIGA screen files to
the SAM. Anyone interested can
drop him a line at the SDC
address below and he will be
happy to explain the procedure
involved. Issue 5 of the SUPPLE-
MENT contained six converted
AMIGA screens and I thought that
ST screens looked brill on the
SAM, but these AMIGA ones were
mind-blowing. Sorry Brian C.

[many of the screens in our own
monthly DEMO-PIX have been AMIGA
pictures, Simon and we have lots
more excellent ones in the pipe-
line! - Brian Cavers]

SDC 57 St.Saviours Road West
Croydon Surrey CR0 2XE
Tel: 081 689 1449

or:

Dave Tonks (home address) 37
Parker Street Bloxwich Walsall
West Midlands WS3 2LE
Tel: 0922 406239

    Best regards to you all,

        Simon Greenfield

From: R.W. Simpson, DERBY

I have operated a Spectrum+3 and
Citizen LSP 120 printer for the
past two and a half years and
the system has given me no cause
for concern. Just before last
Christmas I purchased Tasword+3
software from Lion Computers and
this won't run satisfactorily.

It appears to load correctly but
within five minutes it starts to
misbehave. Commonly one of the
following happens:
 a)the screen goes blank except
   for Amstrad 1982.
 b)vertical bars fill the screen
   accompanied by a message with
   regard to line 170.
 c)the cursor stops flashing and
pieces fall out of the display.

I've been in contact with Lions
and they've replaced the disc on
three occasions but each has
shown similar symptoms. Their
Sales Manager told me they have
tested the discs on a Spectrum
before sending them to me and
have also tested those I have
returned; all "were found to be
functioning perfectly." He added
that they have not had a general
problem with this software and
assumes I have a hardware fault.
I dispute the latter point since
at no other time has a fault
revealed itself and OUTLET in
particular runs without any
problem. Can you cast any light
on this?
        Yours faithfully,
         R.W. Simpson.

To R.W. Simpson from Brian Gaff



Well, you are certainly having
some strange effects! It sounds
like hardware to me though. A
chat to the helpful folk at Tas-
man may help, in case you have a
problem which is known to them.


I had a similar problem to this
when running CP/M. Everything
worked except one program which
would give either error messages
like 'not installed' or 'not
enough RAM', or just lock up. To
cut a long story short, the
problem went away when the gate
array was changed in the +3!

The +3 extra RAM is not normally
used much in Outlet, but in both
CP/M and Tasword +3, it is. It
could be that the page switching
is not always working correctly,
causing the effects you see.
Certainly, the 48K reset points
to this.

If it does turn out to be the
machine, make sure the repair
firm understands that the fault
only appears in Tasword +3 or
they may send it back as OK(I've
seen it happen).

                          - B.G.

From: Derek Burn, BUCKS.

I was very interested in the
letter from Bill Vale,Outlet 41
concerning 'Masterfile' and
'Specmaker'. As I'd long wanted
to run 'Masterfile' on my Coupe,
I decided to print out this
letter to study at leisure and
found a very peculiar problem.

Pages 47, 49 and 50 printed
normally, but page 48 refused to
print. Selecting options T(his)
and A(11) dropped into BASIC
with the error message "4
Subscript wrong 1705: 4" whilst
option S(et) did nothing at all;
starting at page 47, option A
printed page 47 but stopped at
page 48 with the same error
message.

I don't know whether any other
pages in this, or in any other
issue for that matter, give this
problem - I don't like to use
too much paper - but I would
appreciate your comments.

like to know just how Bill
managed to get 'Masterfile'

been completely unsuccessful.

Brian Cavers to Gerhard Behr

Mmmm.. I'm puzzled. BODY OF REV
does exactly what I said in my
reply - namely, it loads the
"dumpld" code and then uses the
command DUMP. There are no
complex procedures to unravel.
Just look at line 400 and you'll
see it simply says DUMP and that
copies the screen! It's strange
that this works on your system
but if you load"dumpld" yourself
and use DUMP it doesn't.

Try loading BODY OF REV and do a
picture and print it out. Now,
with BODY OF REV still loaded,
press ESC, load a SCREEN$ and
enter DUMP. "How can it fail?" I
ask myself.

The vertical elongation is the
opposite of the compression of
the SAM screen making it seem
even worse. If, instead of load-
ing a screen in the foregoing
test you just enter CLS to clear
the screen and CIRCLE 100,100,50
you will see the circle on the
screen is stretched sideways. It
is a design weakness of the SAM
but it can be corrected on some
tv's and monitors by adjusting
the vertical height of the
display.

If you now enter DUMP (and it
works!) you'll see the circle
elongated the other way - in the
vertical! The same is true of a
square. Now POKE 23068,21 and it
should DUMP a true circle.

I'm not sure if the foregoing
will work with FLASH but it may.
Otherwise someone will need to
hack through the code.

Incidentally, POKING 23068,21
reduces the line spacing so it
probably means some lines will
slightly overlap. This may give
slight dark "streaking" on some
pictures. Remember also,the DUMP
command is very poor with many
full-colour screens as it does
not check the palette properly
but just prints 0 as black and
everything else as white!

Let me know how you get on.

Can anyone help with OMNICALC?
                       - Brian

To R. Oldroyd from Brian Gaff



Well, the SAM does hum, even if
the output is taken from the
computer itself. This seems to
be due to the PCB design. It has
just one ground for everything.
Normally, sound circuits are
supposed to have an analogue
ground which is kept separate
from the digital and video parts
of the machine.


Having said that, the majority

From: Mike Haine, LEAMINGTON

Dear Eds.. SAM is superb! OUTLET on SAM excels!

Nice to see the beginnings of SAMCLASS.Perhaps Stephen Wilson can help with a paging problem. In my version of TABLOID for SAM (Just sent off to Brian), I need to access the screen buffer since my prog uses a screen copy technique. To do this I put a short routine at 4004h:-

EX (SP),HL : LD (4800H),HL : LD A,14 : OUT(251),A : LD HL,8000H : LD DE, 4000H : LD BC,O800H : LDIR : LD HL,(4800H): LD A,2 : OUT (251),A : EX (SP),HL:RET

Briefly this aims to store the value in the stack pointer; page the screen buffer page into the HMPR; COPY the bytes from the top 8 lines of the screen into 4000h to 47ffh; page back the original LMPR; recover sp and Return to the calling point.

This works fine if the routine is called from BASIC but if the call is made from m/c SAM resets. Suggestions welcome. How about it Stephen? Correspondence on SAM very welcome.

Mike Haine, Riverside,Welsh Road Offchurch, LEAMINGTON CV33 9AH

> Mike Haine from Stephen Wilson

[Stephen Wilson is our SAM- CLASS programming expert. Readers may also write direct to him at 41 Warrix Avenue, Irvine,Ayrshire,Scotland KA12 0DW for programming help.]

Thanks for the letter, Mike.

Looking at your routine, I can see you understand the paging principle, but there are quite a few (serious), bugs in your program:

Your routine is stored at #4004 so going through your program: you store the value pointed to by the Stack Pointer.

Although,I don't see why - the stack isn't affected during paging unless its being paged! at #4800, then page the screen into High Mem (32768-65535).

You then say you copy the top 8 lines into #4000! - here is the bug (or is it intentional!). You are writing #800 bytes into #4000, and the routine to do it is at #4004 - the routine will be overwritten! (Remember HL= store, DE=DEstination, BC = length), furthermore,you say you want the top 8 lines - a line is 128 bytes in length (Modes 3 +4),8 of these = 1024 bytes or #400. You then page back the value of the HMPR: The original value is 1 not 2!

(SAMCO use the following page no i.e: Page No=INT (address/16384)-1 so you see (32768/16384)=2-1=1 just like the screen=245760

```text
(245760/16384)=15-1=14!
```

You say the routine works from BASIC - it will, but once the LDIR has been executed,the bytes where the LDIR was,is now a copy of the lines, so now the Z80 starts to execute this data! This is why it may crash, but in BASIC it may hit a 201, and return or something, I'm not exactly sure.

Anyway, here's my alternative, hope it helps! - and I hope I have as well!

SCREEN:EQU #8000 COPYBUFFER:EQU #7000 CODESTART:EQU #4000 LENGTH:EQU #0400

10  ORG CODESTART 20  LD HL,TEMPSPSTORE 30  EX (SP),HL 40  OUT (251),A 50  LD HL,SCREEN 60  LD DE,COPYBUFFER 70  LD BC,LENGTH 80  LDIR 90  LD A,1 100 OUT (251),A 110 LD HL,TEMPSPSTORE 120 EX (SP),HL 130 RET 140 TEMPSPSTORE:DW 0

This sets up a buffer at #7000 to act as a store for the lines you have copied. The code is at #4000 and you can store the value at SP, in TEMPSPSTORE. - Watch where your LDIR ends:you stored your (SP) at #4800,it may be overwritten! Watch where your stack is while paging,especially if its near a boundary- remember not to load your code straight into 16384 - the system will crash because you'll have over- written quite a few important stores,like the stack, and the SYS Vars.

- Stephen Wilson

Хотя я и не понимаю зачем — стек не страдает при переключении страниц, если только не переключается страница, где он находится! — ты сохраняешь его по адресу #4800, а затем подключаешь экран в верхнюю память (32768–65535).

Затем ты говоришь, что копируешь верхние 8 строк в #4000! — вот здесь и кроется ошибка (или это так задумано?!). Ты пишешь #800 байт по адресу #4000, а процедура, которая это делает, находится в #4004 — код сам себя перезапишет! (Помни: HL = источник, DE = приёмник, BC = длина). Более того, ты говоришь, что тебе нужны верхние 8 строк — одна строка имеет длину 128 байт (в режимах 3 и 4), 8 таких строк = 1024 байта или #400. Затем ты возвращаешь значение HMPR: исходное значение равно 1, а не 2!

(SAMCO используют следующую формулу номеров страниц: Номер страницы = INT(адрес/16384)-1, так что (32768/16384) = 2-1 = 1, точно так же, как экран = 245760, (245760/16384) = 15-1 = 14!).

Ты говоришь, что из BASIC процедура работает — да, но как только выполнится LDIR, те байты, где находился сам LDIR, теперь заменены копией строк экрана, и Z80 начинает выполнять эти данные! Вот почему всё может сбоить. А в BASIC он может наткнуться на код 201 (RET) и просто вернуться, я точно не уверен.

В любом случае, вот моя альтернатива, надеюсь, поможет!

```text
     SCREEN:EQU #8000
 COPYBUFFER:EQU #7000
  CODESTART:EQU #4000
     LENGTH:EQU #0400

10  ORG CODESTART
20  LD HL,TEMPSPSTORE
30  EX (SP),HL
40  OUT (251),A
50  LD HL,SCREEN
60  LD DE,COPYBUFFER
70  LD BC,LENGTH
80  LDIR
90  LD A,1
100 OUT (251),A
110 LD HL,TEMPSPSTORE
120 EX (SP),HL
130 RET
140 TEMPSPSTORE:DW 0
```

Этот вариант выделяет буфер по адресу #7000 для хранения скопированных строк. Сам код располагается по адресу #4000, и ты можешь сохранять значение из SP в переменной TEMPSPSTORE. Следи за тем, где заканчивается твой LDIR: ты сохранял свой (SP) по адресу #4800, и его могло затереть! Следи за тем, где находится твой стек во время переключения страниц, особенно если он близко к границе. И помни: не загружай свой код прямо в 16384 — система зависнет, потому что ты перезапишешь кучу важных данных, таких как стек и системные переменные.

```text
     AMSTRAD + IBM - DRIVE B

  OFF   ON   ON   OFF  ON   OFF
```

Как указано на последней странице руководства пользователя дисковода (которое, согласен, написано из рук вон плохо), а деталь, о которой MGT упомянуть забыли — это то, что сначала нужно включить +3, а затем дисковод.
